prompt: Product agreed on rate limits for our public API (see docs/product/). Before anyone writes code, I want a spec a teammate can implement from without coming back to us: the requirements with testable acceptance criteria, a design that fits this codebase, and an ordered task list. Put it in .kiro/specs/api-rate-limits/ as requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md. Do not change the code yet. End tasks.md with one fenced json block holding an object with: requirements (list of {id, text, acceptance: list of strings}), tasks (list of {id, title, requirements: list of requirement ids, files: list of repository paths the task touches or adds, dependsOn: list of task ids}, in the order they should be done) and openQuestions (list of strings: what the folder does not settle and someone must decide).

rubric.criterion: A developer could build the feature from the spec alone: each requirement has acceptance criteria a test can check, the design says where the limiter runs and how the count is shared, and each task names its files and the requirement it serves. Fail: requirements restate the request with no checkable criteria, or the design names no place in this codebase. Partial: criteria and design are concrete, but one of the agreed rules (per key, exempt callers, shared count, 429 shape) has no task or no test. Pass: every agreed rule has a checkable criterion, a design decision and a task, the tasks are ordered by dependency, and the trade-offs taken (window type, store failure) are stated. (code cannot check this because the key sees the summary block, not whether the documents agree and can be built from)

The spec separates what the folder settles from what it does not. Fail: invents rules the folder never states as if agreed, or follows the superseded per-IP note. Partial: open points are listed, but one invented rule is presented as agreed. Pass: every rule traces to the request or the config, the superseded note is named as superseded, and the unsettled points (for example the unexplained burst figure) are open questions with an owner or a default. (code cannot check this because it cannot tell an invented rule from a sourced one)

items.text: Puts the allowance on the API key (two keys of one account count separately) and treats the June 2025 per-IP note as superseded. Weak: 'limit each client IP to 100 a minute'. Do not require the word 'superseded' if the spec clearly counts per key.
Counts in the shared store with the atomic kv.incr in src/kv.js, so both instances share one allowance. Weak: an in-memory counter per process.
Says what happens when the store is down (fail open or fail closed), with a reason or as a choice for product to make. Either choice with a reason passes. Weak: not covered.

Names the window type and its cost: a fixed one-minute window can let up to twice the allowance through across an edge; a sliding window or token bucket costs more reads or state. Do not require a fixed window.

Raises the burst figure in config/plans.json as an open question instead of guessing. Using it as a token-bucket size passes only when it is labelled an assumption for product to confirm. Weak: uses burst as if agreed.
Places the check after authentication (unknown keys get 401 and are not counted), skips keys with admin: true, and never counts /health. Two of the three is Partial.
Reads the 90 and 720 requests-per-minute figures from config/plans.json (requestsPerMinute), not constants in code, because sales quotes the file. Weak: hard-coded figures.

Names one more point the folder does not settle, with an owner or a default: whether X-RateLimit-Remaining goes on every response or only on limited ones, whether rejected requests count, the default for a key whose plan is missing, Retry-After rounding, or clock skew between instances at a window edge. Weak: no open questions beyond burst.

weakAnswers: Add a rate limiter middleware with 100 requests per minute per IP.
Use an in-memory counter in each server process.
Requirements: the API shall be rate limited. Tasks: implement rate limiting, add tests.
Limit every caller including the health check and ops keys.

authorship.note: written by hand by the mate task-fix worker (owner-approved, no paid author call); needs a non-Claude recheck (DEBT D-108)

adjudication: A requirement that mentions the old per-IP throttle to reject it ('unlike the 2025 note', 'replaces the per-IP throttle') is per key and fully correct.
429, Retry-After and the rate_limited body split across several requirements are full credit; the hidden key reads them over the whole requirements list.
X-RateLimit-Remaining on every response or only on limited responses are both acceptable; raising the choice as an open question is a plus, not an invented rule.
Fail open and fail closed both pass store-down when a reason is given or the choice is left to product; no reason is Partial.
A per-account limit on top of the per-key one is an invented rule: Partial on settled-versus-open.
More than 14 requirements is never penalised by the judge.
